correctness.rationale: Fulsche–Hagger's Fourier–Weyl identity for true polyanalytic order k gives vanishing quantization iff a tempered Fourier transform is supported on the finite union of Laguerre-zero circles; for k=1 the multiplier has no zeros and quantization is injective for any bounded symbol. For k>=2 isolate roots by smooth compact Fourier cutoffs whose inverse transforms are Schwartz; Young preserves Lp. Because every Laguerre root is simple, each Fourier-localized term solves (Delta+4lambda)u=0 globally. Angular Fourier separation and smoothness at the origin force each mode c_m J_|m|(2sqrt(lambda)r); Jensen plus the oscillatory asymptotic J_m~r^-1/2 rules out any nonzero Lp mode for p<=4, including critical p=4. For p>4 average null plane waves over a root circle to obtain nonzero real bounded a(z)=J0(2sqrt(lambda)|z|), which is in Lp iff p>4. Integrating its cos^4 leading term gives exactly 3/(4pi lambda) log R +O(1) for critical fourth-power mass. No extrapolation from finite roots is used.
residual_risks: The Fourier–Weyl multiplier is a cited published theorem; it is not reproved here.
